items.title: Alcaraz charts course to tennis's summit by downing Djokovic in his theatre
items.description: Carlos Alcaraz has defeated Novak Djokovic in a pulsating Australian Open final, becoming the youngest man with a career Grand Slam in the process.

items.title: 'It's been a great ride': Djokovic hints 2026 could be his last
items.description: He did not go into detail on what he meant, nor did he confirm a plan to retire this year, but he chose his words carefully on centre court.

items.title: Alcaraz wins maiden Australian Open to complete career Grand Slam
items.description: Carlos Alcaraz is the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, beating 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic in the Australian Open final.

items.title: Palmer rejects political influence claim surfaced in Epstein files
items.description: Clive Palmer denies newly surfaced claims that his 2019 federal election campaign was influenced by a senior advisor to US President Donald Trump.

items.title: Gaza's Rafah crossing is set to reopen after being closed since May 2024
items.description: Although Gaza has four other border crossings, they are shared with Israel, many Palestinians see Rafah as their gateway to the world.

items.title: Liberal frontbenchers dismiss prospect of imminent leadership challenge
items.description: Shadow treasurer Ted O'Brien says it is his "assumption" that Liberal frontbencher Angus Taylor still supports Sussan Ley, despite days of speculation that he's planning to challenge for the leadership.

items.title: 'The president loves Stephen': The man by Trump's side changing America
items.description: From a young age, Stephen Miller was campaigning for ideas that were extremely conservative and extremely strange for a teenager from California. Now, he's running Donald Trump's immigration agenda.

items.title: Why the backyard sprinkler is on the climate change frontline
items.description: Billions of litres of water are sprayed onto household gardens every day during summer, allowing cities to stay green. Now water is running low. Has the sprinkler had its day?

items.title: 'We will be recognised': 21-year-old Australian backs his micronation
items.description: Daniel Jackson claims to be the youngest president in the world. The problem is that no other countries recognise him.

items.title: Hundreds of potentially illegal e-bikes purchased through rebate scheme
items.description: Hundreds of illegal, or potentially illegal e-bikes and e-scooters, were purchased under a state government rebate scheme, according to an internal audit that dates back to before the 2024 Queensland election.

items.title: Olympian Michael Klim warned his fiancée she'd met the 'dud version' of him
items.description: Olympian Michael Klim forged his reputation on strength and athleticism. But after being blindsided by an incurable muscle-wasting disease, he was forced to reinvent himself.

items.title: Grammys 2026: Who, what, when, where — and how to watch
items.description: From Kendrick Lamar to Lady Gaga, here are all the nominees and performers to look out for at the Grammys this year.

items.title: What the Beckham family feud reveals about who controls the narrative now
items.description: In a modern crisis, experts say control doesn't always come from speaking louder — but from knowing when, where and how briefly to speak at all.

items.title: People born on Fremantle Bridge bid farewell before demolition
items.description: Eighty people with a special connection to the Fremantle Traffic Bridge, including two people who were born on it, are invited to cross the 86-year-old structure before it is demolished and rebuilt.

items.title: Chia seed trend on social media has experts worried
items.description: The health benefits of chia seeds have been well publicised, but health and internet experts are urging people to not believe everything you see on social media.

items.title: Alex Volkanovski got the moment he wanted at UFC 325
items.description: Alex Volkanovski's win over Diego Lopes at UFC 325 was enough to retain the world featherweight title and give Australia's greatest ever MMA fighter and his fans exactly what they were looking for.

items.title: Lily Allen has made a huge comeback — soon she'll be in Australia
items.description: The British singer made her triumphant return to the annual countdown with two tracks from her latest album West End Girl.

items.title: 'One minute it was daylight, next it was black' — large outback dust storms rolls in
items.description: After more than a month without a single drop of rain, residents living in outback NSW saw a wall of red earth roll in. The large dust storm was well over 100 metres high and several kilometres wide.

items.title: 'I know that I am not throwing': Pakistan spinner's response to Cameron Green's gesture
items.description: Pakistan spinner Usman Tariq responds after Cameron Green appeared to mimic his action in Australia's comprehensive T20 loss in Lahore.

items.title: University campus to be split between housing and open space
items.description: South Australia's premier announces the future of Adelaide University's Magill campus, which sits on the boundary of two marginal Liberal-held electorates.

items.title: Worldwide relay aiming to connect female motorcyclists across the globe
items.description: These women are on a mission to connect all female riders and challenge the motorcycle industry to take them seriously.

items.title: 'A really big threat': US territories brace for Trump's deep sea mining
items.description: A Trump administration push to begin deep-sea mining is gathering momentum — and stirring alarm in United States Pacific territories.

items.title: NT government's national anthem mandate shows appetite for culture wars
items.description: The NT government's national anthem mandate in public schools made headlines this week — but little will be changing on the ground.

items.title: 'Brave' 12yo shark attack victim honoured with paddle-out at North Bondi
items.description: Hundreds of paddle boarders and others journey into the waves of North Bondi to pay tribute to 12-year-old shark victim Nico Antic.

items.title: A GP refused to give Claire weight-loss drugs — but Juniper approved them
items.description: Claire Munch says she was hospitalised with an eating disorder after a telehealth provider approved weight-loss drugs her GP had refused — and that even after she complained, she was later sent marketing promotions.
